Subject: Finova: Performance SLO & Multi-region routing - follow-up

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the detailed call earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary goal: replace current LLM endpoint with Redwood for customer-facing chat and some async document summarization.
- Latency targets (customer expectation): p99 end-to-end for chat flows in each region. We discussed slightly different targets by region due to network realities.
- Throughput/concurrency: bursty traffic with long tails during batch jobs; baseline target ~200 rps aggregate, concurrency up to ~60 per region during peak.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming is required for the chat product (low-latency partial response UX).
- Data residency: EU-generated PII must remain in EU; APAC data should be processed in APAC region where possible.
- Security/compliance: Finova requires 12 months of audit logs and SOC2 evidence (we discussed next steps with security questionnaire).

Proposed SLOs (initial ask from Finova):
- US: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 110ms, p99 < 200ms (end-to-end token latency for 512-token prompts + streaming enabled)
- EU: p50 < 45ms, p95 < 130ms, p99 < 225ms
- APAC: p50 < 70ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 275ms
- Throughput: support sustained 200 rps across regions with auto-scaling to handle 400 rps bursts for 10 min windows
- Concurrency: target support for 60 concurrent streaming sessions per region without degradation

Notes on routing/residency:
- We plan regional routing by source IP/ingress region; EU traffic will be pinned to our EU region and can be configured to never leave the EU for model execution and KV-store caching.
- Fallbacks: if regional capacity is constrained we can route to a nearby region but only after Finova signs off on cross-border processing for that traffic.

Next steps (action items):
1) We'll provide a performance test harness + temporary API key for Finova to run traffic (see Drive link).
2) Redwood will run a controlled perf test next week using the parameters below and share raw metrics.
3) Security team to follow up on SOC2 artifacts and audit-log retention; David, can you take point here?
4) Aditya will start SOW/PO cadence; target commercial terms to align with pilot scope.

Perf test parameters we propose (please confirm):
- Test window: 30 minutes per region
- Traffic profile: 60% chat (streaming, 1–2k tokens total), 40% short generation (<=256 tokens)
- Load: ramp to 200 rps steady state, with 10-minute 400 rps burst
- Concurrency profile: up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions

Attached: Finova_SLO_Worksheet.xlsx (worksheet to capture test inputs), finova-network-topology.png

Can you confirm the SLO numbers above and whether Finova is comfortable with the proposed APAC p99 of 275ms? If APAC needs stricter numbers we can propose a dedicated APAC capacity pool (reserved) at higher cost.

Thanks — I’ll hold on scheduling the perf window until we have confirmation.

Best,

1) APAC p99 at 275ms — is that including network from our users' mobile devices? Our APAC users are sensitive to latency; 275ms might be borderline. If we need 225ms p99 we should evaluate a dedicated APAC pool. Can you sketch the delta in cost and capacity?

2) Streaming: our chat UI expects real-time token streaming with <100ms per-chunk delivery after generation. Is Redwood streaming via SSE/WebSocket with chunk sizes configurable?

3) Data residency: we need confirmation that EU traffic (including intermediate caches like prefix KV) will never leave EU unless explicitly authorized. Also want to confirm audit log retention/timestamps are stored in region.

4) For the perf test, can you confirm whether the test harness will simulate realistic network egress (i.e., from EU, APAC vantage points)? We want representative tail behavior.

If you can answer these, we can confirm dates.

Hi Samir — great questions, answered inline below.

1) APAC p99 and cost tradeoff
- 275ms numbers above include typical network egress/internet variability from APAC to our SG region; that was our conservative estimate for a shared hosted pool. If Finova needs ~225ms p99 we recommend a dedicated APAC capacity pool (reserved GPU capacity in ap-southeast-1). Estimated delta: ~+35–45% on serving costs and an initial one-time provisioning lead time of ~2–3 weeks. Aditya, I can have ops surface a more detailed cost estimate if you want.

2) Streaming implementation
- Redwood supports token-by-token streaming via SSE and WebSockets. Chunk size and flush frequency are configurable; we can tune to target <100ms chunk delivery by increasing flush frequency and reducing batch window for streaming sessions. That will slightly increase compute footprint (lower batching efficiency) but preserves UX.

3) Data residency and caching
- EU routing: we can configure request pins so that (a) model execution, (b) prefix/KV cache and (c) audit logs stay in the EU region. Fallback routing to non-EU will only happen after an explicit Finova exception flag is set. Audit logs retention is configurable; 12 months is supported and logs can be stored in EU-managed S3 with your KMS. David, I'll loop you in for the SOC2 artifact exchange.

4) Perf test vantage points
- Yes — our test harness supports geo-distributed load generators (US west, EU west, APAC SG) so tail behavior will include realistic network variance. We'll include synthetic mobile-like RTT in the test profile.

Perf test parameters (finalized if that works for you):
- Per-region window: 30 minutes
- Load: ramp to 200 rps steady, 10-minute 400 rps burst
- Session mix: 60% streaming chat (1k–2k tokens), 40% short gen (<=256 tokens)
- Concurrency target: 60 streaming sessions per region
- Measurement: collect p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end time to first token, throughput, error rates, and GPU utilization

Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (pricing delta for dedicated pools)

If that looks good, propose we run the tests next Wed (2026-03-31) 09:00–11:00 in each region (overlapping windows). I’ll provision a temporary API key this afternoon and share the Drive link to the harness. Once tests are complete we’ll share raw logs and a summary dashboard.

Thanks —
Marissa
